_notes: HOW TO EDIT: change any text below and commit. Words in {curlyBraces} are filled in automatically by the site (e.g. {totalRooms} = the sum of every stay's "units"); keep them as they are. Text wrapped in *asterisks* is shown in the accent italic style, and \n starts a new line. Image fields hold photo IDs (file names in public/images without the size/extension).

Owner: the "Private bonfire spot right outside" feature applies to The Sierra, French Stoneva, the Classic Huts and Classic Tents only (none at Timber Hill, Kumaon, Grand Imperial or the three luxury rooms).

nearby: things to do around the estate, grouped by drive time (owner's list). Photos are Creative Commons (Wikimedia Commons / Flickr), credited on the page. Where no photo of the exact spot exists, a close stand-in is used and labelled "Representative photo" via credit.note.
driveRoute: the owner's recommended drive from Delhi (from the owner's route graphic); it skips central Dehradun and Mussoorie.

seo: keywords are chosen by search intent (resort/stay + Mussoorie/Kempty Falls + pool, tents, cottages, family, Delhi getaway). Verify volumes in Google Keyword Planner / Search Console once the domain is live; see SEO.md for the full plan.

ways.title: By road
ways.text: From Delhi, take the new Delhi–Dehradun Expressway, then the Dehradun–Paonta Sahib highway via Selaqui, turning off at Langha Road for Kata Patthar, Juddo Dam and Yamuna Pul. About 5.5 hours, without entering central Dehradun or Mussoorie.

ways.title: By air
ways.text: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun, is 84 km away. We can help arrange a cab from the airport on request.

ways.title: By train
ways.text: Dehradun railway station is the nearest railhead. Take a cab via Selaqui and Yamuna Pul, or ask us to arrange one.

distances.heading: From Zephyr Estate
distances.tip: Tip: leave Delhi early to reach by lunch, and keep the last stretch for daylight.

stays.name: The Sierra
stays.short: 1 villa with 2 rooms, a lounge and a dining area. A private home on the ridge.
stays.story: The Sierra is made for families and friends who want to be together without being on top of each other. One villa with two rooms with poster beds, wooden ceilings and stone-clad walls, a glass-walled living room with antique wall art and striking chandeliers, and a dining area of your own for long breakfasts and late card games.

stays.name: The French Stoneva
stays.short: A French room with a signature French bay window and a balcony, on the ground floor.
stays.story: Stoneva is one of our two French rooms, with exactly the same interior design as its twin, French Timber Hill: a hand-cut timber headboard set against an arch of river stone, whitewashed brick, a sunburst mirror and soft wall lights. Its centrepiece is the French bay window, a deep, cushioned seat to curl up in with the green view. Stoneva is on the ground floor and has its own balcony.

stays.name: The French Timber Hill
stays.short: A French room with a French bay window and a balcony, on the first floor.
stays.story: Timber Hill is the twin of French Stoneva, with exactly the same interior design and the same signature French bay window, here looking straight out at the hills. It sits on the first floor and has its own balcony, set with two armchairs for tea with the mountains in front of you.

stays.name: The Kumaon Cottage
stays.short: Traditional wooden interiors and a sit-out area of your own.
stays.story: Built in the spirit of old Kumaoni homes: a wooden ceiling running end to end, hand-cut timber headboards and warm brass lamps, with an ensuite in river stone lit by a skylight. Step out to your own sit-out area with chairs, a cosy corner for a cup of tea with the hills in front of you.

stays.name: The Heaven
stays.short: The first of three identical luxury rooms, on the balcony passage with valley views.
stays.story: The Heaven is the first of our three luxury rooms, all with exactly the same interiors: a carved four-poster bed under a timber ceiling, river-stone walls, a candle-style chandelier and a black-marble ensuite. Step out to the stand-alone balcony passage that runs along the rooms, a beautiful spot to take in the valley. It is a shared passage, not a private balcony, and has no seating.
features: Shared balcony passage with valley views

stays.name: The Classic Hut
stays.short: Cosy stone huts tucked into the forest, each with a small sit-out area for two.
stays.story: Our two Classic Huts are snug stone hideaways with the forest right outside: a wrought-iron bed, a sit-by-the-window corner with two chairs, and a warm, tiled ensuite. Outside, a small sit-out area for two. Simple, characterful and a few steps from the pool and bonfire.

stays.name: The Classic Tent
stays.short: Luxury tents under the fruit trees, with a solid, fully built washroom and a sit-out area of your own.
stays.story: Tent living without roughing it. Our two Classic Tents are luxury tents set among the fruit trees, with a sit-out area, a carved wooden bed under a block-printed canopy and a chandelier. The washroom is solid and fully built, with proper tiled walls and fittings, not a temporary or portable unit. Your own bonfire spot is right outside. Fall asleep to crickets and wake to birdsong.

stays.name: The Grand Imperial Luxury Tent
stays.short: Our most romantic stay: a grand luxury tent with a four-poster bed and a solid, fully built washroom.
stays.story: Our grandest luxury tent: tall, block-printed walls, a wrought-iron four-poster bed, a river-stone feature wall and a crystal chandelier. The washroom is solid and fully built, with a wooden ceiling and a walk-in shower, not a temporary or portable unit. Outside, a covered deck with a lounger looks out over the estate. Ask us about proposal and anniversary set-ups.

experiences.title: Our pools, a rarity in these hills
experiences.text: You won’t find pools like ours anywhere else around here. A blue-mosaic main pool and a kids’ pool sit in the pines, ringed by loungers, umbrellas and canna lilies. Swim by day, then come back after dark when the water glows for drinks, pizza and dinner at the poolside.

experiences.title: Pickleball in the forest
experiences.text: Along with the pools, the estate has its own pickleball court, tucked against a stone wall with the forest all around. Swim, rally, swim again: a favourite for families and friend groups.

experiences.title: Wood-fired pizza workshop
experiences.text: Top your own base with fresh veg and cheese alongside our chef, then watch it blister in our blue-mosaic wood-fired oven, out in the garden under the fairy lights. Eat it hot by the pool or round the fire.

experiences.title: Lavish food, cooked fresh
experiences.text: Breakfast tables laid with fresh juices, fruit and hot toast, brunch by the pool, and dinner spreads of rich curries, dal, rice, raita, fresh salad and hot rotis, finished with something sweet. Every meal is generous and cooked fresh at the estate.

experiences.title: Bonfire under the stars
experiences.text: Gather round the fire circle as the night cools. Bring stories; we bring the warmth.

experiences.title: Open-air movie nights
experiences.text: A screen by the crackling fire pit, fairy lights overhead, blankets, bolsters and your favourite film.

experiences.title: Birthday & party decor
experiences.text: Balloons, a glowing Happy Birthday sign, fairy-lit canopies, candlelit lounges and a dinner table set just for you. Tell us the occasion and we will dress up the garden.

experiences.title: Stargazing from the ridge
experiences.text: Far from city light, the Milky Way rises over the Garhwal hills on clear nights.

experiences.title: High tea in the sun
experiences.text: Fresh bakes, pots of chai and a stone terrace that catches the afternoon light.

faqs.q: What are the check-in and check-out times?
faqs.a: Standard check-in is in the afternoon and check-out is late morning. Share your arrival time when you enquire and we will do our best to accommodate early arrivals.

faqs.q: Can we book the entire estate?
faqs.a: Yes. The Family Retreat option gives your group all 13 rooms (villa, French rooms, cottages, huts and tents) with the estate to yourselves. Ideal for families, friend getaways and small celebrations.

Yes. Breakfast, high tea and lavish dinner spreads are cooked fresh at the estate, and pizzas come out of our wood-fired oven. We also set up poolside, candlelit and bonfire-side dinners. Tell us about any dietary needs when you book.

faqs.q: How do we reach Zephyr Estate?
faqs.a: We are on Kempty Fall Road, 27 km from Mussoorie and 11 km from Kempty Falls. From Delhi it is about 5.5 hours by road (around 309 km): take the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway, then the Dehradun–Paonta Sahib highway via Selaqui, Langha Road, Kata Patthar, Juddo Dam and Yamuna Pul, without entering central Dehradun or Mussoorie.
